task: D9.11 hardening: manager-owned overview DTO, manager-only error shape, checksum gating and per-hop pool source corrections
decision: The D9.11 manager-only DEX overview is hardened so Flask remains a parameter/DTO adapter and Composite Manager owns business projection. Flask now validates manager chain scope and required overview DTO shape, preserves manager selectedProtocols instead of overwriting it with request protocols, refuses malformed manager responses, and returns a dataSource=manager error DTO without legacyUnaffected/enabled shadow fields. Composite Manager now emits selectedProtocols, routeFrameworkSource, marketObservationSource, marketObservationSourceStage and decisionBasis; YC/ZC hop candidates read Candidate Edge pools, Y-Z hop candidates read Candidate Exchange pools; version gating also compares upstream checksums; PnL is complete only when reviewStatus=completed and signedPnl exists; missing-signal counts are per closed-loop row; unresolved token counts cover loop, YZ and pool references. Existing D9.11 evidence remains unmodified and this report records the correction as a separate evidence item.
corrections: Flask overview errors use a manager-only DTO with dataSource=manager and no legacyUnaffected/enabled fields
Flask validates chainId and required overview arrays/objects and does not silently invent missing business fields
Manager selectedProtocols is preserved; request protocols are exposed only as requestedProtocols
Composite Manager emits top-level routeFrameworkSource, marketObservationSource, marketObservationSourceStage and decisionBasis
Y-Z hop candidates now use Candidate Exchange pool snapshots while YC/ZC continue to use Candidate Edge pool snapshots
Overview version consistency checks downstream and upstream checksums, not only version numbers
Overview PnL completion requires reviewStatus=completed plus signedPnl; missing signed PnL is counted per closed loop
Unresolved token accounting covers closed-loop, YZ and pool references
Library version/checksum fallback reads the nearest non-empty upstream manager state instead of closing on a disabled downstream status
